commands.name: agent.attachPreset
commands.summary: Attaches `presets` (library presets; `engram:/default` turns the Default slot on) after the `after` preset in call order (else at the end). Applies what it can: each one it cannot attach is in `skipped` with why (`not-found`, `wrong-kind`, `already-present`, `item-path-invalid`). CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (a library preset named while the library cannot be read) · `root-generation-stale` applies nothing.

commands.name: agent.cancelQueuedInput
commands.summary: Cancels one entry of the waiting list (the same command as the ✕ on screen) — `outcome` = `cancelled` (withdrawn right away) | `requested` (a cancel was requested — the list shows the outcome). An id not on the list is NOT_FOUND. CONFLICT = the name is ambiguous (two or more with the same name — point at it by id) or a connected viewer holds this agent's input (try again after it lets go).

commands.name: agent.detachPreset
commands.summary: Detaches `presets` (every attached entry of each; `engram:/default` turns the Default slot off — CONFLICT `default-preset-detach` unless `yes`). Detaching what is not attached changes nothing; an entry that is not a library path is matched by its exact text, and one that matches nothing refuses, INVALID_ARGUMENT `item-path-invalid`. CONFLICT `root-generation-stale`.

commands.name: agent.duplicate
commands.summary: Registers a copy of an agent beside it (the same parent), asleep, named after it with the next number (`bob` → `bob(1)`): the same backend, mode, folder, env and presets, with no conversation or history. INVALID_ARGUMENT when this surface does not create the original's backend; CONFLICT at the roster ceiling. After a timeout or an unknown outcome, check `agent.list` before calling again.

commands.name: agent.interrupt
commands.summary: Interrupts the running turn (≠ kill — the process lives). `outcome` = `requested` (the interrupt was sent — whether the turn actually stopped is announced by the turn-end event). NOT_FOUND = no such agent or it is asleep. CONFLICT = the name is ambiguous · there is no turn to interrupt · this agent does not support interrupt · a connected viewer holds this agent's input.

commands.name: agent.list
commands.summary: The whole roster — name · liveness · working folder · parent — and the state of the roster store (`store`).

commands.name: agent.listQueuedInputs
commands.summary: The list of inputs a live agent received mid-turn without confirmation yet that they were accepted (non-terminal only). `state` = `queued` (before confirmation — we hold it or handed it to the agent and wait for the outcome. codex hands it over by steer when the running turn's tool ends, or to the next turn if the turn ends without a tool · claude hands it to the CLI queue right away) | `sent` (codex handed it to the agent and waits for the echo saying it was received — cancelling does not remove it) | `unconfirmed` (handed over but unknown whether it was accepted — it stays on the list and mail waits for that outcome, and cancelling removes it right away · ★no backend emits it today★ — that stage of codex was removed, ADR-0235) | `cancelling` (a cancel was requested — stays until the agent produces an outcome). `cancel.answer` = `none` (no answer yet) | `not_removed` (the agent answered it could not remove it, or the request failed) · `cancel.vendor_closed` = the agent already closed that entry. `stopped_after_error` = the previous turn ended with a real error and no turn has ended successfully since — meanwhile mail does not go in automatically (kernel `last_end_failed`). User text codex holds may go out again the moment new user text comes in (ADR-0235 decision 4). An asleep agent holds no list (NOT_FOUND).

commands.name: agent.move
commands.summary: Changes the parent in the tree.

commands.name: agent.new
commands.summary: Registers a new agent in the roster (does not launch it — it stays asleep). `presets` are judged as `agent.attachPreset` judges them: the agent is created with what can be attached, each one left out is in `skipped` with why. CONFLICT `library-unavailable` (a library preset named while the library cannot be read) or `root-generation-stale` creates nothing.

commands.name: agent.presets
commands.summary: An agent's presets: the Default slot, the attached presets, its working folder and why it is locked, its backend and mode, `base_rev`, and the folders, conflicts, problems and notices a launch would meet — it leaves out the `missing` problem rows (and a `library_unavailable` row for a library folder that is not set or not there) and refuses on the others.

commands.name: agent.rename
commands.summary: Changes the display name.

commands.name: agent.reorderPresets
commands.summary: Puts the attached presets in `order` — every entry `agent.presets` shows, each once (a duplicate as often as it is attached), else INVALID_ARGUMENT `reorder-order-mismatch` with the expected order in `args`. `base_rev` = the `base_rev` you read; CONFLICT `rev-mismatch` = the attachments changed since (read them again). The Default slot is untouched. CONFLICT `root-generation-stale`.

commands.name: agent.resolve
commands.summary: Resolves 1–8 words pointing at agents (name or id) at once — `agents` is in the same order as the request. The resolving rules are the same as other verbs taking `target` (exact id match first · then exact name match — case-sensitive · asleep agents included). `live` = `state` of `agent.list` is `live`. If even one cannot be resolved, it returns no line and fails. The text of a failure caused by one word always starts with `targets[i]: ` (i = that word's position counting from 0) — INVALID_ARGUMENT = an empty word (only whitespace) · NOT_FOUND = no such agent (the trailing `candidates` of the text = names worth choosing, in name order · `none` if the roster is empty) · CONFLICT = that name exists two or more times (the trailing `candidates` of the text = those ids — call again by id). If the count is outside 1–8, it is INVALID_ARGUMENT without that head.

commands.name: agent.setWorkspace
commands.summary: Changes an agent's working folder. `cwd` must be an existing absolute folder, else INVALID_ARGUMENT `workspace-not-found` {cwd, why} — `why` also says `not absolute`, or that the folder did not answer in time (`timeout`), could not be read, or is on a network share that is not reachable (`share not reachable`). Only an asleep agent that has never conversed can change it: CONFLICT `workspace-locked` {reason: `running` | `preparing` | `conversed` | `changing`}. The agent keeps its name.

commands.name: agent.spawn
commands.summary: Starts an agent: wakes an existing one (`target`) or creates one in `cwd` and starts it. A preset item that is not found, or a library folder that is not set or not there, does not block: it is left out and named in `notices`. A blocked launch starts nothing and is `CONFLICT` with `args.reasons`, one row per reason by `kind`: `broken` {kind, item, via, code, args, line?} (a folder entry that cannot be read included) · `conflict` {kind, items: [{item, via}], code, args, line?} · `library_unavailable` {kind, code, args, line?} (a library folder that exists but cannot be read). Fix the listed items, then start again. With `cwd`, a launch blocked before the agent is added answers `CONFLICT` with `args.reasons` and creates nothing; a start failure after the add is `INTERNAL` with `args.agent_id` (plus `args.reasons` when blocked) — start that agent by target, do not create another.

commands.name: library.folders
commands.summary: Every folder of the library, flat, by path; a skill folder is marked `skill`. CONFLICT `library-unavailable` when the library cannot be read (no root, or the root cannot be walked).

commands.name: library.list
commands.summary: The items directly in `folder` (unspecified = the root) and its plain subfolders. `query` searches name and description (case-insensitive) in every item below `folder` and answers matching rows only (no `folders`). `kinds` keeps only those kinds (unspecified or empty = all; a broken file counts as the kind it claims; a skill's `SKILL.md` matches only `SkillFile`). `builtins` also answers the built-in preset `engram:/default` in `builtins`, under the same filters. A `folder` at or below a link answers one `path-through-link` row, which the filters do not apply to. CONFLICT `library-unavailable` when the library cannot be read.

commands.name: library.newFile
commands.summary: Creates file `name` of `kind` in `folder` (unspecified = the root) from an empty template (`.md` or `.yaml` is added unless the name ends with it); answers its path. Refusals as `library.newFolder`.

commands.name: library.newFolder
commands.summary: Creates folder `name` in `parent` (unspecified = the root); answers its path. CONFLICT `name-exists` (nothing replaced) · `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed` (a retry after it may answer `name-exists` — the partial file or folder stays); NOT_FOUND `not-found` = the parent is missing.

commands.name: library.read
commands.summary: One item's detail: its row, its file on disk (`absolute`), the presets that list it (`presets_direct`) or reach it through nested presets (`presets_indirect`), the agents that attach it (`agents_direct` — a preset only) or a preset reaching it (`agents_indirect`), an instruction's `excerpt` and a settings file's field names (`settings_fields`). NOT_FOUND `not-found` = no such item; CONFLICT `library-unavailable`.

commands.name: library.refresh
commands.summary: Re-reads `folder` (unspecified = the whole library) from disk and reports it: `changed` items, `problems` of the files re-read, `no_kind` (yaml files with no `kind` — not listed), `skipped_links` (links not entered) and `errors` (where reading failed — those items are kept as they were; a row with no `path` = the root listing or a folder that is not read failed). Use it after changing library files outside Engram. It never refuses except for a `folder` that is not a library path (INVALID_ARGUMENT `item-path-invalid`).

commands.name: library.relink
commands.summary: Re-points every reference to `from` (in preset files, then agents) at `to`; when `from` is missing it also re-points the other missing items of `from`'s folder whose names are in `to`'s folder (`more` of them). Answers the pairs `fixed`, the files `written`, the files `skipped` with why, and `stopped` when an IO failure stopped it after a write (run the same relink again once it is cleared). NOT_FOUND `not-found` = `to` is not in the library; INVALID_ARGUMENT `relink-kind-mismatch` = `to` is of another kind than its references need; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale`.

commands.name: library.setRoot
commands.summary: Points the library at the absolute folder `path` (`create` makes the folder first; no file is copied or moved) and saves it in library.json; answers the status after the change (as `library.status`). CONFLICT: `library-config-read-only` (nothing done), `library-root-unusable` (the folder cannot be used — nothing published), `library-config-write-failed` (the new root is live but not saved). A relative path is INVALID_ARGUMENT `item-path-invalid`.

commands.name: library.status
commands.summary: The library root now: `root` (`null` = unset), `root_setting` = `default` | `explicit` (`null` when library.json could not be read), `state` = `unset` | `ok` | `missing` (not there or not a folder) | `unreadable` (there but cannot be read or did not answer) (+ `state_why`), `config` (library.json) = `ok` | `read_only` | `corrupt` | `unsaved` (+ `config_why`), `suggested_new` = the default place. `root_generation` = pass it to an edit, which then refuses if the root changed since (CONFLICT `root-generation-stale`). CONFLICT `library-unavailable` only from a daemon that runs no library.

commands.name: preset.add
commands.summary: Adds `items` (each into the list of its kind, `backend` for all of them) or absolute `folders` — one of the two — after the `after` entry (else at the end). Applies what it can: each item it cannot add is in `skipped` with why (`not-found`, `wrong-kind`, `already-present`, `preset-cycle`, a backend word it does not take …). A bad folder refuses the whole call, INVALID_ARGUMENT `preset-folders-refused` naming each. NOT_FOUND `not-found` = no such preset file; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: preset.check
commands.summary: Judges a draft of the preset's lists as `preset.save` would, without writing: the folders it would list, the conflicts and problems a launch of it would meet, and `save_refuses` = a save of this draft would be refused (each mismatch is a `broken` problem with `args` `{path, list}`). `folders` omitted = the file's folders stay. CONFLICT `library-unavailable`.

commands.name: preset.get
commands.summary: A preset's entries with their state, its folder entries, the conflicts and problems a launch of it alone would meet, its edition `rev` and how many agents attach it. `path` = a library path or `engram:/default`. NOT_FOUND `not-found`; INVALID_ARGUMENT `wrong-kind` (not a preset); CONFLICT `library-unavailable`.

commands.name: preset.previewFolder
commands.summary: What a folder entry would load: the absolute `folder` normalized (`path`, `null` = not absolute), why `preset.add` would refuse it (`refused`), and per backend (`backend`, unspecified = every one) and mode (`mode`, unspecified = both) what that backend loads from it. `truncated` = the listing stopped at its cap, `skipped` = entries it could not read, `unlisted` = why a folder that exists could not be listed. Reads only. INVALID_ARGUMENT `backend-tag-unknown`; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` only from a daemon that runs no library.

commands.name: preset.remove
commands.summary: Removes `items` (every entry of each, in every list) or `folders` — one of the two; removing what is not there changes nothing. Answers the preset after the change. NOT_FOUND `not-found` = no such preset file; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: preset.reorder
commands.summary: Puts one `section` in `order` — every entry `preset.get` shows in it, each once (a duplicate as often as it is listed), else INVALID_ARGUMENT `reorder-order-mismatch` with the expected order in `args`. `base_rev` = the `rev` you read; CONFLICT `rev-mismatch` = the file changed since (read it again). NOT_FOUND `not-found`; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: preset.save
commands.summary: Replaces the four lists (and `folders`, when given — omitted = they stay) with the draft, all or nothing: any mismatch (not a path, an unknown backend word, one item twice in a list, an item of another kind, a cycle, a relative folder …) refuses the whole save, INVALID_ARGUMENT `preset-save-refused` listing each. A missing item is allowed. `base_rev` (optional) = the `rev` you read; CONFLICT `rev-mismatch` = the file changed since. NOT_FOUND `not-found`; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: preset.setBackend
commands.summary: Sets the backend of `items` in instructions and skills (`backend` unspecified = every backend). Applies what it can: an item the preset does not list, or lists only in presets or settings, is in `skipped`. An unknown backend word refuses the whole call, INVALID_ARGUMENT `backend-tag-unknown`. NOT_FOUND `not-found`; CONFLICT `library-unavailable` · `root-generation-stale` · `library-write-failed`.

commands.name: usage.get
commands.summary: The usage limits of one backend (5-hour · weekly · per-model weekly) — the values the daemon holds. If the next automatic query time has passed, it launches a query here (or attaches to one in progress) and waits up to 5 seconds for it to end — past that it answers with the held value with `in_flight` = true and the query continues. `served` = `Fresh` (a value fetched by the query this request waited for) | `Cached`. `state` = `Ready` | `NotInstalled` | `NeedsLogin` | `Unavailable` (this account has no limit info — no windows are carried) | `Failed` (`next_attempt_in_secs` = until the next automatic query) | `Rejected` (upstream refused — until `retry_in_secs` passes, even `usage.refresh` does not query). Even on failure, the windows are the last known values. The cause of an abnormal state = `detail_kind` (category word) · `detail_code` (the number upstream gave) · `upstream` (upstream original text — secrets masked · 200 chars). A window's `left_pct` = the amount left (`used_pct` is the amount used), and `null` means unknown (not 0). Time fields are relative seconds as of the moment of answering, and only `resets_at` is epoch seconds. A backend whose field this daemon does not hold is NOT_FOUND.

commands.name: usage.refresh
commands.summary: Forces a new query of the usage limits (the same command as ⟳ on screen) — launches a query (or attaches to one in progress) and waits up to 5 seconds for it to end, answering with the same row as `usage.get`. There is no call interval limit — it queries again even if the previous query just ended, and if frequent, upstream may refuse (that refusal may show only as `Failed`, not `Rejected`). Answering with the held value (`Cached`) without querying = the upstream refusal period remains (even if a value came in during the refusal and `state` is `Ready`, the period remains — `retry_in_secs` is not carried then). Even if the query fails or does not end within 5 seconds, it is `Cached` (the query did go out then). The meaning of the fields is the same as `usage.get`. A backend whose field this daemon does not hold is NOT_FOUND.
